id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

name.description: User specified name of this monitoring job.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

groups.description: Model monitoring groups to run in this job.

models.description:
List of {@link MlModel}s to be monitored.
The performance metrics will be calculated per {@link MlModel}.
There may be further grouping of performance metrics within a single {@link MlModel} based on @link MlModel.Monitor.Group#groupBy}.

title:
Represents a monitoring job for performance monitoring of many {@link MlModel}s. All models should be within the scope of a single
{@link MlProject}.
Monitoring groups are specified in a list of {@link MlModel.Monitor.Group}. Each model monitoring metric result will be persisted as a
{@link MlModel.Monitor.TimedResult}, and the execution metadata is persisted as {@link MlModel.Monitor.BatchResult}.

See {@link MlModel.Monitor.Group}
See {@link MlModel.Monitor.Data}


Usage:
```python
# Define monitor groups for a multi-output MlModel with two predictions - "sales" and "revenue".
monitor_group_for_sales = c3.MlModel.Monitor.Group(metrics={"accuracy": c3.MlAccuracyMetric(), "recall": c3.MlRecallMetric()},
                                                   inputs=c3.MonitorExample.SalesData(),
                                                   filter="region=USA",
                                                   groupBy="state")
monitor_group_for_revenue = c3.MlModel.Monitor.Group(metrics={"mse": c3.MlMeanSquaredErrorMetric()},
                                                     inputs=c3.MonitorExample.RevenueData())

# Create a monitoring job
monitoring_job = c3.MlModel.Monitor.Job.fromModels(models=[MlModel1, MlModel2],
                                                   groups=[monitor_group_for_sales, monitor_group_for_revenue],
                                                   )

# Manually trigger the monitoring job
operation_run = monitoring_job.start()
monitor_job_run = operation_run.result()
monitor_results = monitor_job_run.monitorResults()
```
Execution details for a single execution of monitoring job.
Assumption:  prediction data is available for continent of North America.
For `monitor_group_for_sales` - Prediction data for non-USA region is not used for model performance
as per filter specification. If the prediction data is available for 50 states in USA, one score per state per model
will be calculated as `groupBy` is specified. i.e There will be 50 accuracies for `MlModel1` (one per state) and
50 recalls for `MlModel1` (one per state).
Similarly, there will be 50 accuracies for `MlModel2` (one per state) and 50 recalls for `MlModel2` (one per state).
Hence, there will be 200 entries in {@link MlModel.Monitor.TimedResult} for `monitor_group_for_sales`.

For `monitor_group_for_revenue` - All the predictions are used as there is no filter.
No further segmenting of scores was necessary as `groupBy` is not provided.
There is one score per model. i.e one `mse` for `MlModel1` and one `mse` for `MlModel2`.
Thus, there will be 2 entries in {@link MlModel.Monitor.TimedResult} for `monitor_group_for_revenue`.
name: MlModel.Monitor.Job
